headline.purpose: The largest type in the product. Page titles and empty states; nothing sits above it.

body.purpose: Prose, descriptions, transcript text. The default reading size at 14px.

control.purpose: The workhorse. Buttons, inputs, selects, nav rows, breadcrumbs. Thirteen pixels, not fourteen.

label.purpose: Uppercase sidebar section headers, panel captions, column names. Small, spaced, quiet.

code.purpose: Geist Mono for anything read character by character: identifiers, branches, counts, diffs, harness output.

shadows.name: edge-highlight
shadows.purpose: The primary depth cue. A dark panel without this reads as a hole cut in the page.

shadows.name: edge-highlight-control
shadows.purpose: The same trick at greater strength on filled controls, so a primary button reads as raised.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: A surface lifted off the field that still belongs to the layout. Cards, docked panels.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: Genuinely detached and temporary. Dialogs, popovers, the command palette, a dragged card.

motion.name: control
motion.purpose: Button and input state transitions. Paired with a 1px active translate that composites.

motion.name: nav
motion.purpose: Colour transitions on rail items and navigator rows.

motion.name: card-entrance
motion.value: 200ms ease-out, fade plus one-step slide from top
motion.purpose: A card mounting into a board column, including after a successful move.

motion.name: node-reflow
motion.purpose: A workflow node sliding to a new position, so the eye follows a card after a delete or insert. Suppressed while dragging.

motion.name: spinner
motion.purpose: A single control someone is actively waiting on. Linear because easing makes a spinner look like it is labouring.

motion.name: spinner-ambient
motion.purpose: The calm cadence for boards where many spinners turn at once. A dozen brisk ones read as agitation.

motion.name: thinking
motion.value: 1.4s ease-in-out infinite, dots staggered 0.18s and 0.36s, 2px travel
motion.purpose: A model composing, watched for minutes. Slower than either spinner on purpose.

motion.name: edge-flow
motion.purpose: A workflow edge showing the direction the pipeline runs.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: 0.01ms for all animation and transition, except spinner and thinking dots which switch to brightness-only keyframes
motion.purpose: Reduced motion asks for less movement, not for less meaning. The two indicators keep indicating.

shell.name: control-ladder
shell.purpose: Every control height. Default 32. Inputs, selects and the command bar share these numbers.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled emphasis in the system. Rarely more than one per screen.
components.css: .ds-btn { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 6px; height: 32px; padding: 0 12px; border: none; border-radius: 8px; font-family: var(--font-geist-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.25rem; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; user-select: none; transition: background-color 100ms ease-out, border-color 100ms ease-out, color 100ms ease-out, transform 100ms ease-out; } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring, oklch(0.556 0 0)); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary, oklch(0.922 0 0)); color: var(--primary-foreground, oklch(0.205 0 0)); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 0 oklch(1 0 0 / 18%); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, oklch(0.922 0 0)) 90%, transparent); } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--primary, oklch(0.922 0 0)) 95%, transparent); }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The default secondary action. Warms its border toward the ring on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.985 0 0)); border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(1 0 0 / 10%)); } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--accent, oklch(0.371 0 0)); border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, oklch(0.556 0 0)) 40%, transparent); } .ds-btn-outline:active { background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent, oklch(0.371 0 0)) 80%, transparent); }

components.name: Loading Button
components.description: Loading is built into the button, not left to call sites, so a pending review decision cannot be submitted twice.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn ds-btn-primary" aria-busy="true" disabled><svg class="ds-spinner" width="14" height="14" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M21 12a9 9 0 1 1-6.219-8.56"/></svg>Approving</button>
components.css: .ds-spinner { animation: ds-spin 1.1s linear infinite; flex-shrink: 0; } @keyframes ds-spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } } .ds-btn[disabled] { pointer-events: none; opacity: 0.45; } .ds-btn[disabled]:active { transform: none; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-spinner { animation: ds-breathe 2s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-breathe { 50% { opacity: 0.35; } } }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: 32px so a field and the button beside it share a baseline exactly. One focus outline, no second ring.
components.html: <input class="ds-input" type="text" placeholder="Search issues" aria-label="Search issues">
components.css: .ds-input { height: 32px; width: 100%; min-width: 0; padding: 4px 10px; border: 1px solid var(--input, oklch(1 0 0 / 15%)); border-radius: 8px; background: color-mix(in oklab, var(--background, oklch(0.145 0 0)) 40%, transparent); color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.985 0 0)); font-family: var(--font-geist-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 0.8125rem; line-height: 1.25rem; outline: none; transition: color 100ms, background-color 100ms, border-color 100ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.708 0 0)) 70%, transparent); } .ds-input:hover { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, oklch(0.556 0 0)) 30%, transparent); } .ds-input:focus-visible { border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--ring, oklch(0.556 0 0)) 50%, transparent); outline: 2px solid var(--ring, oklch(0.556 0 0)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Task State Badge
components.description: The signature component. Soft fill mixed into the surface, its own glyph, and its label. Shown here in Review, the only state waiting on a person.
components.html: Review
components.css: .ds-state-badge { display: inline-flex; width: fit-content; flex-shrink: 0; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 2px 8px; border: 1px solid; border-radius: 999px; font-family: var(--font-geist-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 500; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-state-badge svg { flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-state-review { color: var(--state-review, oklch(0.78 0.15 70)); background-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--state-review, oklch(0.78 0.15 70)) 8%, var(--background, oklch(0.145 0 0))); border-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--state-review, oklch(0.78 0.15 70)) 10%, var(--background, oklch(0.145 0 0))); }

components.name: Board Column Header
components.description: A signature surface. Washed in its state colour at 10% with a 2px rule of that colour at full strength across the top, so a column reads from across the room.
components.html: Review3
components.css: .ds-column-head { position: relative; display: flex; flex-shrink: 0; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 12px 12px 10px; border-bottom: 1px solid color-mix(in oklab, var(--border, oklch(1 0 0 / 10%)) 60%, transparent); background-color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--state-review, oklch(0.78 0.15 70)) 10%, transparent); font-family: var(--font-geist-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-column-rule { position: absolute; inset-inline: 0; top: 0; height: 2px; background: var(--state-review, oklch(0.78 0.15 70)); } .ds-column-icon { color: var(--state-review, oklch(0.78 0.15 70)); flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-column-label { font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.12em; text-transform: uppercase; color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground, oklch(0.985 0 0)) 80%, transparent); } .ds-column-count { margin-left: auto; font-family: var(--font-geist-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 0.6875rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.708 0 0)); }

components.name: Panel Card
components.description: One step above the field, hairline bordered, lit along the top edge.
components.html:
Harness profile
Claude Code, subscription mode, concurrency cap 3.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 24px; border: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(1 0 0 / 10%)); border-radius: 14px; background: var(--card, oklch(0.205 0 0)); color: var(--card-foreground, oklch(0.985 0 0)); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 0 oklch(1 0 0 / 5%), 0 1px 2px oklch(0 0 0 / 40%), 0 8px 24px oklch(0 0 0 / 22%); font-family: var(--font-geist-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-card-title { font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.5rem; } .ds-card-desc { font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.375rem; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.708 0 0)); }

components.name: Activity Rail Item
components.description: A 48px rail slot. The active marker is a bar on the rail's edge, not a filled pill, so it reads from the periphery.
components.css: .ds-rail { display: flex; width: 48px; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 10px 0; border-right: 1px solid var(--border, oklch(1 0 0 / 10%)); background: var(--sidebar, oklch(0.205 0 0)); } .ds-rail-item { position: relative; display: flex; width: 32px; height: 32px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border-radius: 10px; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.708 0 0)); transition: color 150ms, background-color 150ms; } .ds-rail-item:hover { color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.985 0 0)); background: var(--accent, oklch(0.371 0 0)); } .ds-rail-item--active { color: var(--foreground, oklch(0.985 0 0)); } .ds-rail-marker { position: absolute; left: -10px; width: 2px; height: 18px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--foreground, oklch(0.985 0 0)); } .ds-rail-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--ring, oklch(0.556 0 0)); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Step Marker
components.description: A workflow step in the strip. Colour is never alone: the marker carries its number, or a glyph for the states that are not simply a position.

components.css: .ds-steps { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; gap: 6px 12px; margin: 0; padding: 0; list-style: none; font-family: var(--font-geist-sans, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-step { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; } .ds-step-marker { position: relative; display: flex; width: 20px; height: 20px; flex-shrink: 0; align-items: center; justify-content: center; border: 1px solid; border-radius: 999px; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-step-upcoming { border-color: var(--border, oklch(1 0 0 / 10%)); background: var(--background, oklch(0.145 0 0)); color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.708 0 0)); } .ds-step-done { border-color: var(--state-done, oklch(0.75 0.15 150)); background: var(--state-done, oklch(0.75 0.15 150)); color: var(--background, oklch(0.145 0 0)); } .ds-step-running { border-color: var(--state-running, oklch(0.75 0.13 240)); background: var(--state-running, oklch(0.75 0.13 240)); color: var(--background, oklch(0.145 0 0)); box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in oklab, var(--state-running, oklch(0.75 0.13 240)) 20%, transparent); } .ds-step-label { max-width: 16rem; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--muted-foreground, oklch(0.708 0 0)); } .ds-step-label-done { color: color-mix(in oklab, var(--foreground, oklch(0.985 0 0)) 80%, transparent); } .ds-step-label-running { font-weight: 500; color: var(--state-running, oklch(0.75 0.13 240)); } .ds-sr { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; }

narrative.overview:
SoloW is an instrument panel for work that runs without you watching it. Its chrome is deliberately colourless: every surface, border, and control token in the theme sits at chroma zero, pure greyscale, because the interface's entire job is to make one thing findable at a glance across seven columns of parallel work. That thing is state. Colour is therefore spent almost nowhere and hoarded for three narrow signal families, of which the seven Task lifecycle hues are the loudest. A reader who looks up from their editor should be able to tell, from the corner of their eye and without reading a word, whether anything is waiting on them.

The register is precise, quiet, and mechanical, and it is dense the way professional tooling is dense. Type is pitched down a full step from document sizes, controls sit on a four-pixel ladder, numbers are tabular so a count changing in place does not shift its neighbours, and every button depresses by exactly one pixel when pressed. Nothing here is hurried. The spinners run at two different speeds depending on how many might be on screen at once, and the thinking indicator is slower than either, because an operator watches it for minutes at a time and a brisk rhythm at that duration reads as agitation rather than work.

Depth is made with light rather than shadow. A dark panel with no lit edge reads as a hole cut in the page, so surfaces carry a one-pixel inset highlight along the top; shadows exist but are ambient support, not the mechanism. A fine film grain sits over the whole viewport at under three percent, which is enough to stop wide dark fields banding into plastic and to give the surface a material quality without ever becoming a texture anyone notices. The shell is a VS Code shape, five fixed regions, and that is a promise about how the product is used: open all day, beside something else, never the only window.
keyCharacteristics: Chroma-zero chrome; hue reserved for state, diff, and provider signals
Dark-first, shipped dark-only, with a complete light token set held in reserve
Console density: 13px control text, 24px status bar, 44px header
Depth by lit edge, not by shadow
Every state carries a hue, a glyph, and a word, never colour alone
Motion is decoration everywhere except the two indicators where it is the information

rules.name: The Chroma-Zero Chrome Rule
rules.body: Every surface, text, border, and control token is chroma 0. A blue-violet cast was removed from this theme by explicit decision. Do not reintroduce hue into the chrome to suggest elevation, grouping, or brand; elevation is made with lightness and light.

rules.name: The Three Families Rule
rules.body: Task lifecycle, diff, and provider state are three separate colour families. They may look similar (two greens, two reds) and they must never share a token. They answer unrelated questions, and one of them changing must not drag the others with it.

rules.name: The Never Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: No state is ever communicated by hue alone. Every one carries its own icon and an accessible word as well (WCAG 1.4.1). If a new state cannot be given a distinct glyph, it is not ready to ship.

rules.name: The Thirteen-Pixel Rule
rules.body: The sm step is 13px, not Tailwind's default 14. Fourteen is a document size; this is read in a panel beside an editor. The named steps are redefined at the theme so vendored components inherit the pitch for free, and there is exactly one place to change it. Never reach for an arbitrary bracket size to get back to a document scale.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can change in place is tabular-nums: column counts, durations, token totals, step indices. A count that reflows its neighbours when it ticks from 9 to 10 is a bug, not a detail.

rules.name: The No Display Type Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the app is larger than 1.125rem. A hero-sized heading in an operating surface is a marketing gesture that has wandered in from a landing page.

rules.name: The Four-Pixel Ladder Rule
rules.body: Controls are 24 / 28 / 32 / 36. A new control that needs a height picks one of those four; it does not invent a fifth. This is what makes a row of mixed controls sit on one line without optical correction.

rules.name: The One Scroll Region Rule
rules.body: The app scrolls in exactly one place. A surface that introduces a second page-level scrollbar has a positioning bug, not a layout preference.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: A dark panel gets a lit top edge or it reads as a hole. Reach for the highlight before reaching for a shadow, always.

rules.name: The Two Shadows Rule
rules.body: There are two elevations, panel and float, and no others. If a surface seems to need a third, it is either a panel or a float and the question is which.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one focus treatment in the app, a 2px outline at 2px offset on :focus-visible only, so a mouse user never sees it. Components do not bring their own.

rules.name: The Soft Badge Rule
rules.body: Badges mix their colour into the surface, never into transparent. One definition, in the components layer, serves every badge in the product.

rules.name: The Indicating Motion Exception
rules.body: Reduced motion switches everything off except the spinner and the thinking dots, whose movement is the only thing separating "still working" from "hung". Those keep indicating by brightness instead: no transform, nothing that travels. Reduced motion asks for less movement, not for less meaning.

dos: Do keep chrome at chroma 0 and spend hue only on the three signal families. The greyscale is a decision the codebase already made once, on the record.
Do give every new state a glyph and an accessible word alongside its hue. Colour alone fails a colour-blind reader, and these distinctions are the product.
Do pick control heights from the ladder: 24, 28, 32, or 36. Default to 32.
Do reach for the lit top edge before a shadow when a surface needs to sit forward.
Do use tabular-nums on any number that changes in place.
Do route new badges through the soft-badge definition rather than writing a filled pill.
Do let the component own its loading state, so a pending action cannot be double-clicked.
Do target WCAG 2.2 AA, the standard recorded in PRODUCT.md, including the keyboard drag path on the board and the reduced-motion behaviour above.
donts: Don't import a vendor theme or third-party palette. The syntax highlighting is written in this app's own tokens precisely so a GitHub-blue keyword never sits beside this product's indigo and makes the transcript read as two products stapled together.

Don't bring marketing-page gestures into operating surfaces: no hero sections, no display type above 1.125rem, no decorative gradients. The two faint radial washes behind the sign-in card are the single deliberate exception, and they exist because that screen is a lone card on an otherwise empty field.
Don't let the lifecycle, diff, and provider colour families share a token, however similar two of them look.
Don't add a second focus ring, a second scroll region, or a second definition of "soft".
Don't ease a spinner. Linear is the considered choice here, not the lazy one.
Don't speed up the thinking indicator. Its unhurried rhythm is what separates a model composing from a stalled network request, watched over minutes.

Don't repeat a Task's lifecycle state as a badge on a card that already sits in the column for that state. The column says it; a pill on every card is seven columns of noise. Review is the one exception, and it earns it by being the only state waiting on a person.
